title: Trace locks, journals, and checkpoints around one database file
description: Switch scenarios to see what readers and the single writer use in rollback and WAL modes, then inspect the operational consequence.

nodes.label: Reader connections
nodes.detail: Each reader holds a transaction snapshot. Long-lived reads can delay a rollback-mode writer or prevent a WAL checkpoint from fully advancing.

nodes.label: Single writer
nodes.detail: One connection at a time changes the database. Keep its transaction short and use a bounded busy policy for contention.

nodes.label: SQLite pager
nodes.detail: Coordinates page cache, locks, atomic commit, rollback, and durability through the operating-system storage interface.

nodes.label: Main database
nodes.detail: Contains the database pages. In WAL mode, recent committed pages may remain in the WAL until a checkpoint copies them back.

nodes.label: Rollback journal
nodes.detail: Rollback mode records original page content before the main file changes so an interrupted transaction can be reversed.

nodes.label: WAL + shared memory
nodes.detail: WAL mode appends committed pages and uses shared state to coordinate readers, the writer, and checkpoints on one host.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.detail: Copies eligible committed pages from the WAL into the main database. Active readers can limit how far it advances.

scenarios.label: Rollback-mode read
scenarios.summary: Several readers hold shared locks while a writer prepares a change using the rollback journal.
scenarios.result: Readers can coexist, but the writer eventually needs the required lock to commit. A long read can extend writer wait, so transaction lifetime matters.

scenarios.label: WAL reader + writer
scenarios.summary: Readers use a stable snapshot while the single writer appends committed pages to the WAL.
scenarios.result: Readers and one writer overlap, reducing a common source of blocking. Writes remain serialized and the WAL still needs a checkpoint policy.

scenarios.label: Long WAL reader
scenarios.summary: A reader keeps an old snapshot while new writes continue to append and checkpoints attempt to advance.
scenarios.result: The checkpoint cannot pass pages needed by the old snapshot, so the WAL can keep growing. Find and bound long read transactions rather than deleting WAL files.

scenarios.label: Shared network file
scenarios.summary: Processes on different machines attempt to coordinate one WAL-mode database through a mounted network filesystem.
scenarios.result: WAL depends on same-host shared coordination and is not a multi-machine write design. Put a service owner in front of local SQLite or choose a client/server database.
